description: This pie chart, titled “Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse,” visually represents the distribution of media outlets categorized by their influence or presence in political discourse, with each slice corresponding to a specific outlet or group and labeled with a numerical value indicating its relative share. The chart is divided into 15 distinct slices, each assigned a unique color and labeled with the name of the outlet or category. The largest segment is “Other,” occupying 13% of the chart and colored gray, followed by “The Daily Caller” at 8% (green), “Drudge Report” at 8% (orange), and “The Huffington Post” at 7% (red). Other notable segments include “NPR” and “Vox” at 6% each (purple and brown), “The Guardian” and “BBC” at 5% each (pink and gray), and “RT,” “Daily Kos,” “National Review,” “Daily Mail,” “Red State,” “Fox News,” “CNN,” and “Shareblue/PoliticoUSA” each at 3% (various shades of blue, green, and purple). The chart includes a legend on the right side, which is grayed out and appears to be a placeholder, and all percentage values are displayed directly within the corresponding slices. The segments are arranged in a clockwise descending order by size, starting from the top right.
